newsitem.title: GERMANY: Currencies underpin Bremen cotton prices.
newsitem.headline: Currencies underpin Bremen cotton prices.

text.p: Cotton prices quoted in the Bremen market gained from recent dollar firmness versus European currencies and what was seen as a bullish U.S. cotton survey, the Bremen Cotton Exchange said in a fortnightly report.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture on August 13 forecast U.S. 1997 cotton output one percent lower than in its July forecast and six percent below 1996.
Yarn spinners were looking for nearby cotton ahead of the new crop amid limited ex-trade offers and fading origin quotes.
Spot sales were limited to Central Asian standards two and three.
The Exchange reported sales for 1997 and 1998 shipment in West African and Central Asian 1 and 2 standards and Greek cotton.
Shipment for second half 1997 was agreed in Syrian and Sudanese-Acala origins, Indian and Australian varieties for the third quarter, and Peru-Tanguis for Nov/Dec 1997.
